subject: maths
title: Addition and Subtraction within 20
seo_title: Year 1 Addition and Subtraction within 20 Worksheets: Number Sentences and Missing Numbers
standard_text: Read, write and interpret mathematical statements involving addition (+), subtraction (−) and equals (=) signs; add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero; solve one-step problems that involve addition and subtraction, using concrete objects and pictorial representations, and missing number problems such as 7 = ? − 9.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction within 20: add with pictures and a number track, take away and count back, read number sentences with +, − and =, find missing numbers and solve simple word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Add: count on. Take away: count back. = means “is the same as”.
key_sub: 9 + 3: say 9, then count 10, 11, 12. 12 − 5: go back to 10, then 3 more to 7. For 7 = ? − 9, put the 9 back: 7 + 9 = 16.
body_html:
Adding: put together

Adding means putting groups together. The sign is +. Say “add” or “plus”.

You can count all of them. Or start at the first number and count on.

Count on

6 + 4 = ?

Say 6. Then count 4 more: 7, 8, 9, 10.

Answer: 10

Subtracting: take away

Subtracting means taking away. The sign is −. Say “take away” or “minus”.

You can also count back on a number line.

Reading number sentences

A number sentence uses numbers and signs. = means “is the same as”. Both sides of the = have the same value.

SignSayExample
+add, plus4 + 3 = 7
−take away, minus9 − 2 = 7
=equals, is the same as7 = 4 + 3

Adding 0 or taking away 0 does not change a number: 6 + 0 = 6 and 6 − 0 = 6.

Missing numbers

Sometimes a number is missing. Use the other two numbers to find it.

Missing number

? + 4 = 9

Something add 4 makes 9. Take the 4 away: 9 − 4 = 5.

Answer: 5

Missing number

7 = ? − 9

Which number take away 9 leaves 7? Put the 9 back: 7 + 9 = 16. Check: 16 − 9 = 7.

Answer: 16

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start number: 9 + 3 → “9, 10, 11”, so 11Say 9, then count 3 more: 10, 11, 12. 9 + 3 = 12
Adding when you should take away: 12 − 5 = 17Look at the sign. − means take away: 12 − 5 = 7
Taking the small digit from the big one: 12 − 5 = 13Go back to 10 first: 12 − 2 = 10, then 10 − 3 = 7
Writing the total as the missing number: 4 + ? = 9 → 9Ask: 4 add what makes 9? 4 + 5 = 9, so 5
Thinking = means “the answer comes next”= means “is the same as”. 9 = 4 + 5 is true

faq.q: What addition and subtraction does a Year 1 child learn?
faq.a: In Year 1, children add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero. They read and write number sentences with +, − and =, and solve simple problems and missing number questions such as 7 = ? − 9.

faq.q: How do you explain the equals sign to a Year 1 child?
faq.a: Say that = means “is the same as”, not “the answer comes next”. Show that 4 + 3 = 7 and 7 = 4 + 3 are both true because each side has the same value.

faq.q: What is a number track in Year 1 maths?
faq.a: A number track is a row of numbered squares. Children put a finger on the first number and jump on or back, counting the jumps but not the starting square.

faq.q: How can I help my child with missing number problems?
faq.a: Use the two numbers you know. For ? + 4 = 9, take 4 from 9 to get 5. For 7 = ? − 9, add 7 and 9 to get 16, then check that 16 − 9 = 7.

items.q: What does the = sign mean?
items.e: = means is the same as. Both sides have the same value: 4 + 3 = 7 and 7 = 4 + 3.

items.q: Which one says “eleven take away three equals eight”?
items.e: Eleven is 11. Take away is −. Three is 3. Equals is =. Eight is 8. 11 − 3 = 8.

items.q: Which one says “six add seven equals thirteen”?
items.e: Add is +. Equals is =. Thirteen is 13: 1 ten and 3 ones. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q: Which one says “twenty is equal to twelve add eight”?
items.e: Write the words in order. Twenty, is equal to, twelve, add, eight: 20 = 12 + 8.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
items.e: 9 + 6: start at 9 and count on 6: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. 9 + 6 = 15 is true.

items.q: Look at both sides of the =. Which one is true?
items.e: 8 + 6 = 14. The = can come first: 14 = 8 + 6 is true.

items.q: Check each one. Which is true?
items.e: Think addition: 9 + 8 = 17. So 17 − 9 = 8 is true.

items.q: Which number sentence is NOT true?
items.e: 13 − 4 is 9, not 8. So 13 − 4 = 8 is not true. The other three are true.

items.q: 12 = 7 + 5. Which one means the same?
items.e: = means “is the same as”. You can swap the two sides: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: 10 − 3 = 7. Which one means the same?
items.e: Swap the two sides of the =. 10 − 3 is the same as 7: 7 = 10 − 3.

items.q: There are 6 ducks on a pond. 5 more ducks land. How many ducks are on the pond now?
items.e: More come, so add. Start at 6. Count on 5: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. Do not count the 6. 6 + 5 = 11.

items.q: Ruby has 9 toy cars. She gets 6 more for her birthday. How many toy cars does she have now?
items.e: More cars, so add. 9 + 1 = 10, and 5 more is 15. 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: There are 14 ducks on a pond. 6 ducks fly away. How many ducks are left?
items.e: Some go away, so subtract. Go back to 10 first: 14 − 4 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: There are 15 biscuits on a plate. The children eat 7. How many biscuits are left?
items.e: Eaten biscuits are gone, so subtract. Go back to 10 first: 15 − 5 = 10. Then take away 2 more: 10 − 2 = 8.

items.q: Harry has 12 apples. He gives 4 to Gran. How many apples does he have now?
items.e: Giving away means subtract. Start at 12. Count back 4: 11, 10, 9, 8. Do not count the 12. 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: Evie has 8 stickers. Isla has 7 stickers. How many stickers do they have altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 8 + 7 is 1 more than 7 + 7 = 14. 8 + 7 = 15.

items.q: There are 17 people on a bus. 5 people get off. How many people are on the bus now?
items.e: Getting off means subtract. 17 is 10 and 7. 7 − 5 = 2. 10 and 2 is 12. 17 − 5 = 12.

items.q: A bag has 10 red sweets and 9 yellow sweets. How many sweets are in the bag?
items.e: Put the two colours together, so add. 10 + 9 is 1 ten and 9 ones. 10 + 9 = 19.

items.q: Poppy has 20p. She spends 6p on a lolly. How much money does she have left?
items.e: Spending means subtract. 20 − 6: 20 is 10 and 10. 10 − 6 = 4. 10 and 4 is 14. So 14p.

items.q: Amelia reads 7 pages before lunch. She reads 8 pages after lunch. How many pages does she read?
items.e: Put the pages together, so add. 7 + 7 = 14, and 8 is 1 more than 7. 7 + 8 = 15.

items.q: There are 19 books on a shelf. The class takes 5 books. How many books are left?
items.e: Taking books away means subtract. 19 is 10 and 9. 9 − 5 = 4. 10 and 4 is 14. 19 − 5 = 14.

items.q: Zara is 6. Her brother is 3 years older. How old is her brother?
items.e: Older means more years, so add. Start at 6. Count on 3: 7, 8, 9. 6 + 3 = 9.

items.q: Ethan has 6 conkers. He wants 13. How many more conkers does he need?
There are 11 children in the playground. Some go inside. Now there are 4. How many children went inside?
items.e: Think: 11 − ? = 4. Count up from 4 to 11: 4 + 7 = 11. So 7 children went inside.

items.q: Some ducks are on a pond. 5 more ducks come. Now there are 12 ducks. How many ducks were there at the start?
items.e: Think: ? + 5 = 12. Take away the 5 that came: 12 − 5 = 7. Check: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Noah has 13 marbles. Arjun has 8 marbles. How many more marbles does Noah have than Arjun?
items.e: Find the difference. Count up from 8 to 13: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 5 more.

items.q: There are 16 pencils in a pot. 9 are blue. The rest are red. How many pencils are red?
items.e: Think: 9 + ? = 16. 9 + 1 = 10, then 6 more is 16. 1 + 6 = 7. So 7 are red.

items.q: 18 children are in a class. 3 are away today. How many are at school? Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 3 children are away, so take them away from 18. 18 − 3 = 15.

items.q: Maya has 5 balloons. She gets 9 more. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: She gets more, so add. 5 + 9 = 14.

items.q: Alfie has 15 grapes. He eats some. Now he has 9. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: He starts with 15. He eats some, so take away. 9 are left, so he ate 6: 15 − 6 = 9.
